script.base: LV is a 3.5-point home favorite in a closed dome with a 41.5 total and a 22.5 implied team total, so the book expects a one-score game, not a shootout and not a 20-point blowout. Base flow: Las Vegas leads or stays within a score, pace stays modest, and the offense leans on Ashton Jeanty (52 carries and 268 rush yards in weeks 3-5, about 17 carries a game) because Brock Bowers is out and the total does not require a pass-heavy script. Tennessee, implied 19.0, can run Tony Pollard early (44 carries, 176 yards in that same window) but, as a 3.5-point dog, throws more if it trails; Blake Hance is out and JC Latham is questionable, so that passing stays short rather than becoming a Ridley/Ayomanor shot game. Both starting backs should finish. Starters late snaps are not a blowout risk at only -3.5.
script.flip1: Las Vegas jumps ahead by more than a field goal. Jeanty runs the clock and the rush over gets safer unless the lead gets large enough that Raheem Mostert (only 11 carries and 84 yards in three games) or Zamir White (5 carries, 19 yards) vultures late snaps. Tennessee abandons the run, so Pollard rush and rush-plus-rec unders cash, and Cam Ward deep shots to Calvin Ridley (291 air yards in three games) and Elic Ayomanor (179 air yards) stall.
script.flip2: Tennessee hangs around or leads. Pollard keeps a full carry share and the 78.5 rush-plus-rec under is the leg that dies, especially with his weeks 3-5 rush-plus-rec path already at 59, then 76, then 78. Jeanty still faces a Titans run defense at 5.32 yards per carry, so efficiency can cover a few fewer carries, but the over is less comfortable. Ward throws more and the live overs become Ridley, Chigoziem Okonkwo and Ayomanor, which this slip does not bet.

The Raiders bleed left and middle and are sound on the right, which is the hook/middle/slot area if they are zone-heavy, not the outside right corner. matchup.pressure: Las Vegas blitz rate is 26 percent. Tennessee EPA per dropback is -0.49 versus the blitz and -0.14 with no blitz, so Cam Ward is materially worse when blitzed. That pressure, plus Hance out and Latham questionable, kills deep wide-receiver yards and boosts running-back and tight-end checkdowns. Tennessee blitz rate is 24 percent. Las Vegas EPA per dropback is -0.23 versus the blitz and +0.01 with no blitz, so Smith is only mildly worse when blitzed and Arden Key being out trims Titans pressure further.

Raiders run defense is the sturdier unit at 4.11 yards per carry and only 12 runs of 10-plus, with 12 passes of 20-plus for 170 yards, and the pass bleed is left and middle rather than right.
matchup.overlap: The overlap that is the core of an edge is Ashton Jeanty, 52 carries and 268 yards at 5.15 yards per carry in weeks 3-5, into a Titans run defense allowing 5.32 yards per carry and 20 explosive runs, with edge Arden Key out. The secondary overlap, Calvin Ridley and his 291 air yards into the Raiders left and middle yards-per-attempt bleed, is real on the chart and cut by Ward blitz EPA and the Titans offensive-line injuries, so it is not a leg. Brock Bowers being out means the Titans middle bleed (7.18) is no longer a Bowers problem; it is a Meyers, Tucker and Jeanty-checkdown problem, and Marcus Harris is the missing corner on that side.

pre_mortem: It is Monday and this lost because Tennessee loaded the box on a Bowers-less Raiders offense, Arden Key being out did not loosen the edge, and Jeanty finished in the 40s the way the 43-yard game already showed he can, with a 63.5 number leaving no room after a 63-yard game in this very window. Pollard under lost because the game stayed a one-score rock fight in the dome, Van Jefferson was inactive, JC Latham played the whole game, and Pollard got 18 to 20 touches. His recent rush-plus-rec path was already 59, then 76, then 78, and Las Vegas has allowed 12 runs of 10-plus, so one crease clears 78.5. No closing price was available, so even a right read could have been a bad number against a season-median stand-in rather than a real market.
slip_story: One story only: Las Vegas controls a low-total dome game and runs it, and Tennessee cannot match that efficiency on a healthier Raiders front. The slip is two legs, no touchdowns, one market per player: Ashton Jeanty rush yards over 63.5 with Tony Pollard rush-plus-rec under 78.5. Do not add Calvin Ridley, Elic Ayomanor, Tre Tucker or Jakobi Meyers overs, because those need the shootout or the Tennessee-leads flip. Do not pair a game under with same-game wide-receiver overs. Not a 3-to-4 leg ticket because only these two cleared the read. Not sized, and not a bet.
